evidence: FY2025 financial statements received an unqualified audit opinion and no material restatement was identified in the supplied 10-K.
The Q2 2026 filing separates operating results from large unrealized equity-security gains.
Alphabet generated approximately $185.7 billion of TTM operating cash flow and held $242.5 billion of cash and short-term marketable securities at June 2026.

Despite that liquidity, it raised $49.6 billion net equity and preferred capital through June, issued $51.8 billion of debt in H1, and issued another $25.0 billion of notes in August to fund an extraordinary AI infrastructure cycle.
vetoes.resolution_needed: Establish that external financing is temporary and that AI infrastructure can generate returns above the cost of capital without recurring equity issuance after 2027.

evidence: Common shares outstanding increased from 12.088 billion at December 2025 to 12.230 billion at June 2026.
Mandatory convertible preferred stock can add common shares by 2029, and a $40.0 billion ATM remained unused and available at June 2026.
TTM SBC was approximately $28.1 billion.
vetoes.resolution_needed: Track quarterly fully diluted shares, ATM issuance, preferred conversion economics, buybacks and FCF per share through the capex peak.

evidence: Search, subscriptions and Cloud growth are accompanied by strong consolidated and segment operating profits.
Cloud operating margin expanded materially while revenue accelerated.
Cloud margin expansion is strong positive evidence for incremental economics.
FY2025 FCF was nearly flat year over year and H1 2026 FCF fell to about $4.3 billion as capex doubled, so consolidated incremental ROIC is not yet observable.
Management expects 2027 capex to increase significantly again from the 2026 $180-$190 billion range.
vetoes.resolution_needed: Obtain evidence of utilization, incremental gross profit, asset useful life and FCF-per-share recovery for the 2026-2027 investment cohorts.

evidence: Search revenue grew 17% in Q2 2026 and AI usage expanded, arguing against current shrinkage.
US Search remedies and ad-tech litigation may weaken default distribution, data advantages and publisher-tool economics.
vetoes.resolution_needed: Monitor commercial-query share, TAC, default placement, mandated data sharing and post-remedy Search monetization.

evidence: Current price is approximately equal to the modeled Base value rather than requiring the modeled Bull case.
Implied ten-year revenue growth of roughly 11%-14% is demanding but not unrealistic given current 20%+ growth.
More than 70% of FY2025 revenue came from advertising and Search remains the central profit engine.
Cloud, subscriptions and YouTube provide meaningful and fast-growing diversification but are not yet enough to make Search impairment immaterial.
vetoes.resolution_needed: Confirm that Cloud and subscriptions continue increasing their share of durable operating profit while Search withstands AI and regulatory changes.

evidence: Liquidity and operating cash flow make insolvency remote.
Permanent loss is more plausibly caused by prolonged low returns on AI capital, Search erosion and dilution than by bankruptcy.
